Sitting atop the kidneys, this pair of endocrine glands produces hormones including adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol. What organ is it?
Adrenal gland (also known as suprarenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.
Its type species, a common freshwater organism constantly studied in classrooms and labs, lends its name to an entire genus of shape-changing single-celled organisms — what's the genus?
Amoeba (genus) is a genus of single-celled amoeboids in the family Amoebidae.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
From starch that stores energy to the cellulose that stiffens plants and the chitin in insect shells, this biomolecule family is essentially sugars and their derivatives — what is it?
Carbohydrate is a sugar (saccharide) or a sugar derivative.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

Produced by a mammal's mammary glands in the first days after birth, this antibody-rich milk helps protect newborns like calves and human infants from infection before regular milk takes over — which substance?
Colostrum (from Latin, of unknown origin), also known as foremilk, is the milk expressed by the mammary glands of a female mammal during the first few days following delivery of the newborn.
Mostly aquatic mandibulate arthropods, this group spans shrimp, crayfish, copepods, and barnacles — and modern science now files insects in alongside them — what are they?
Crustacean (from Latin word "crustacea" meaning: "those with shells" or "crusted ones") are mandibulate arthropods that are traditionally a part of the paraphyletic subphylum Crustacea.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.
This is the only surviving member of its order, the Proboscidea, and its tusks are actually overgrown incisor teeth used as both weapons and tools — what animal is it?
Elephant are the largest living land animals.
This ground-nesting songbird of Europe and the Palearctic sings its signature tune while hovering high over farmland and heath, and now also breeds in Australia and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
This genus in the rose family includes more than 20 species prized for their sweet-to-tart edible fruits, with domestic hybrids grown worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Fragaria is a genus of flowering plants in the rose family, Rosaceae, commonly known as strawberries for their edible fruits.
Before he founded a piece of the U.S. aircraft industry, this pioneer set an unofficial world speed record astride a V8-powered motorcycle that stood unbroken until 1911. Who was he?
Glenn Curtiss (May 21, 1878 - July 23, 1930) was an American aviation and motorcycling pioneer, and a founder of the U.S.
Caused by a group of enteroviruses, this common infection opens with a fever and then sprinkles blistering spots on exactly the three body parts named in its label. What is it?
Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common infection caused by a group of enteroviruses. It typically begins with a fever and feeling generally unwell.
This small rodent, with a pointed snout and a long, nearly hairless tail, has thrived by living alongside humans to the point that truly wild populations are now rare — what animal is it?
House mouse (Mus musculus) is a small mammal of the rodent family Muridae, characteristically having a pointed snout, large rounded ears, and a long and almost hairless tail.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Known as the sunroot or earth apple, this central-North-American member of the sunflower family is cultivated for its tuber rather than its bloom — what is it?
Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America.
This American biologist and one-time Communist Party member had four husbands, the last being the physicist who led Los Alamos — who was she?
Kitty Oppenheimer (ne Puening; August 8, 1910 - October 27, 1972) was an American biologist, botanist, and a member of the Communist Party of America until leaving in the 1930s.
Viruses muddy its definition, and it might exist beyond Earth in unfamiliar forms — but on this planet it fills air, water and soil, even harsh niches of extremophiles. What is it?
Life is the capacity, in matter, for processes such as cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, cell growth, adaptation, response to stimuli, and reproduction.
This alpha-amino acid, a building block for many proteins, carries a side chain that stays partially charged at the body's normal pH, classifying it among the basic amino acids — what is it?
Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an -amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

These aquatic insects carry ancient traits from the first flying insects — long tails and wings that won't fold flat — and their water-dwelling young are a living signal of clean, unpolluted streams; what bug is this?
Mayfly (also up-winged flies or up-wing flies, or drake-flies in the UK; shadflies or fishflies in northern U.S.

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.

This genus of fragrant flowering shrubs, native to Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean, is widely grown as an ornamental in Hawaii and in desert climates of the Arabian Peninsula — name the genus?
Plumeria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.
This Eurasian fruit tree, also called the cherry plum, is believed to be one of the ancestral parents of the plum we cultivate today — what species is it?
Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum.
This biological process by which new organisms are produced from parents comes in two forms — one requiring a single organism, the other requiring two. What is it?
Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms - offspring - are produced from their parent or parents.

Originally conceived in the 1960s as a jet trainer before evolving into a supersonic strike aircraft, this joint British-French warplane — retired by both original operators — remains in service only with the Indian Air Force. Name it?
SEPECAT Jaguar is a British-French supersonic jet attack aircraft originally used by the British Royal Air Force and the French Air Force in the close air support and nuclear strike role.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
Native to a swath from Ireland to southern China, this aromatic herb is used to flavor food and herbal teas, and its extracted oil serves as both a flavoring and a scent — what is it?

Spearmint (Mentha spicata), also known as garden mint, common mint, lamb mint and mackerel mint, is native to Europe and southern temperate Asia, extending from Ireland in the west to southern China in the east.
This Chinese physician and revolutionary led the 1911 Revolution, overthrew the Qing dynasty, and founded the Republic of China as its first president. Who was he?
Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 - 12 March 1925) was a Chinese physician, revolutionary and political philosopher who founded the Republic of China (ROC) and the Kuomintang (KMT).
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Native to Central and South America but now found in sub-Saharan Africa, which parasitic flea burrows into skin to cause the condition tungiasis?
Tunga penetrans is a species of flea also known as the jigger, jigger flea, chigoe, chigo, chigoe flea, chigo flea, nigua, sand flea, or burrowing flea.

Manufactured under license by both Goodyear and Brewster during World War II, this American carrier-based fighter aircraft became one of the most capable fighter-bombers of the war and later saw service in Korea — which aircraft?
Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War.
Also called humped cattle for the fatty growth on its shoulders, this South Asian breed group is used for everything from plowing to dairy, and even kept as pets in miniature form — what is it?
Zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.

Typically affecting women between 35 and 50, this uterine condition occurs when endometrial-like tissue grows within the muscular wall of the uterus, causing painful, heavy periods — what is it called?
Adenomyosis: Extension of endometrial tissue into the myometrium.
On 18 March 1965, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first person to walk in space, spending over twelve minutes outside his capsule during a Voskhod mission — who is he?
Caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, this intestinal infection can spread to the liver and trigger abscesses there even without any prior diarrhea — what condition is it?
Amoebiasis: Human disease caused by amoeba protists.
NATO codenamed 'Cub,' this four-engine Soviet turboprop served for three decades as the standard cargo and paratroop transport of the Soviet Air Forces — which aircraft?
Antonov An-12: Soviet medium-range transport aircraft.
Caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides and spread through food tainted with eggs, this infection most often hits children and is symptomless in over 85% of cases — what is it?
Ascariasis: Disease caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The eggs hatch in the intestines, the larvae burrow through the gut wall, and migrate to the lungs via the blood.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
Coined in 1814 by chemist William Hyde Wollaston, this polyatomic anion forms when carbonic acid loses a proton and plays a crucial role buffering the body's pH — what is it?
Bicarbonate: Polyatomic anion. It is a polyatomic anion with the chemical formula HCO−3.

Flying for the U.S. Air Force since 1955, this subsonic strategic bomber evolved from a six-turboprop straight-wing design into eight swept-wing turbojets and can haul up to 70,000 pounds of weapons — what's its name?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress: American strategic bomber aircraft.

This Italian-American physicist invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to prove cosmic rays arrive more strongly from the West than the East, before Italy's racial laws forced him to flee — who was he?
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)
A heavy-set, fox-like canid native to East Asia, this animal is named for its raccoon-like face markings and is unusual among canids for hibernating in winter and climbing trees. What is this animal?
Common raccoon dog: Canid indigenous to East Asia. Named for its raccoon-like face markings, it is most closely related to foxes.
Stalked ones anchored to the seafloor are nicknamed 'sea lilies' while the free-swimming kind are 'feather stars' — what's the class name for these mouth-on-top echinoderms?

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Nicknamed the spiny anteater, this quill-covered, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has babies called puggles — which creature?

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
With a bushy tail, triangular ears, and a reputation for cunning that echoes through folklore worldwide, which small omnivorous canid lives on every continent except Antarctica?
One of Maxwell's equations, this application of the divergence theorem connects electric charge distribution to the electric field it creates. Which one is it?
Gauss's law: Foundational law of electromagnetism relating electric field and charge distributions.
One of the very first animals domesticated — in Iran some 10,000 years ago — this Bovidae cousin of the sheep now numbers over 1.1 billion worldwide, 150 million of them in India; what is it?

This French civil engineer made his name building railway bridges like the Garabit Viaduct and later helped erect the Statue of Liberty, before retiring to study meteorology and aerodynamics — who was he?
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)
Named from a Tongan and Marquesan word meaning 'bitter,' this pepper-family plant's ground root becomes a ceremonial Pacific Islands drink that numbs the mouth — what is it?
Kava: Species of plant. Kava or kava kava (Piper methysticum: Latin 'pepper' and Latinized Greek 'intoxicating') is a plant in the pepper family, native to the Pacific Islands.
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
Mostly black on top, white below, and sporting unmistakable white eye patches, this cosmopolitan apex predator is actually the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family. What is it?
Orca: Largest living species of dolphin.
Secreted by small neck glands when blood calcium runs low, this peptide messenger raises calcium levels and boosts active vitamin D production — which one?
Parathyroid hormone: Mammalian protein found in humans.
Discovered in 1972 and used to treat scabies and lice, this pyrethroid insecticide is safe for most mammals but especially dangerous to cats, who metabolize it slowly — what is it?
Permethrin: Medication and insecticide. It is applied to the skin as a cream or lotion.
Linked to prolonged sitting and excess hair, which skin condition causes a cyst to form between the cheeks of the buttocks and is treated with incision and drainage?
Pilonidal disease: Skin infection between the buttocks. Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Soft enough to slice with a knife, this silvery alkali metal carries the symbol K and takes its name from potash, the plant ashes it was first isolated from — what element is it?
Potassium: Chemical element with atomic number 19 (K)
Crossing the line between the natural and social sciences, this discipline scientifically studies the mind and behavior — both conscious and unconscious — in humans and other animals. What is it?
Psychology: Study of mental functions and behaviors.
Also marketed as canola once bred to lower its naturally high erucic acid content, this yellow-flowered Brassicaceae crop is the world's third-largest source of vegetable oil — which plant?
Rapeseed: Plant species grown for its oil-rich seed.
Usually caused by a vitamin-D deficiency, this childhood condition softens bones and can produce bowed legs and stunted growth — the adult analogue is osteomalacia; what is it?
Named after the Latin word for willow tree, from which it was first derived, this plant hormone and aspirin precursor shows up in anti-acne cosmetics — what is it?
Salicylic acid: Chemical compound used in medicines and industry.
With an eagle-like body perched on crane-like legs and a bare red-orange face, which African bird of prey spends most of its time hunting on foot across the savanna?
Secretarybird: Bird of prey. The secretarybird or secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
In this rare congenital condition affecting about 1 in 10,000 people, the heart and other major organs sit as a mirror image of their normal position — what's it called?
Situs inversus: Condition in which organs are reversed.

Encased by the vertebral column and running from the brainstem down to about the first lumbar vertebra, this hollow, fluid-filled structure forms the other half of the central nervous system alongside the brain — what is it?
Spinal cord: Part of the vertebral column in animals.

Native to New Guinea and domesticated by Papuan and Austronesian peoples, this tall grass with sucrose-rich stalks was carried across the Pacific and eventually to India and China in ancient times. What crop is it?
Sugarcane: Several species of grass used for sugar production.
Also known as estragon, this perennial herb in the daisy family comes in a French variety prized for cooking and a milder Russian variety — which herb?
Tarragon: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
The body's primary muscle of respiration, this dome-shaped sheet separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and contracts to pull air into the lungs — what is it?
Thoracic diaphragm: Sheet of internal skeletal muscle.
Approved in the US in 1981, this sedating antidepressant from the SARI class racked up more than 24 million prescriptions in 2023, making it the fifth most common antidepressant — what is it?
Trazodone: Antidepressant medication. Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Roughly 20 to 30 centimeters long in adults, this smooth-muscle tube carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder — what is it called?
Ureter: Tubes used in the urinary system in most animals.
Comprising the mons pubis, labia, clitoris, and vaginal opening, these external structures of the female genitalia are supplied by the pudendal arteries. What is this collectively called?
Vulva: External genitalia of the female mammal. The folds of the outer and inner labia provide a double layer of protection for the vagina (which leads to the uterus).
Nicknamed 'Superman syndrome,' this genetic condition gives males an extra Y chromosome, often extra height but usually normal fertility — which one?
XYY syndrome: Genetic condition in which a male has an extra Y chromosome.

The symbol for radium is Ra. Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
